beats.title: Lesson 14 — Catching the Intrusion
beats.say: Welcome back to CybICS. A real intrusion is rarely a single action. It is a chain: reconnaissance, then access, then impact. In this lesson the intrusion detection system correlates that chain into one verdict.

beats.head: One alert is noise; a chain is an intrusion
beats.body:
A single alert can be a false alarm. What convinces a defender is a pattern of activity from one source over time.
  • The CybICS IDS counts distinct detections from an attacker.
  • Once enough fire, it raises an intrusion verdict and unlocks the flag.
  • We will chain a scan and a write flood — recon and impact — from the attack machine.
beats.say: A single alert can be a false alarm. What convinces a defender is a pattern of activity from one source over time. The CybICS intrusion detection system counts distinct detections from an attacker, and once enough fire, it raises an intrusion verdict and unlocks the flag. We will chain two very different attacks, a scan and a write flood, recon and impact, both from the attack machine.

beats.caption: Attack 1 of 2: reconnaissance - a port scan
beats.say: First, reconnaissance. We scan the OpenP L C. That trips the port scan and S Y N flood rules, two detections tied to our source address.

beats.caption: Attack 2 of 2: impact - the Modbus write flood
beats.say: Then impact. We flood the high pressure tank register, the attack from lesson six. That trips the Modbus flood and the unauthorized write rules, two more detections from the same source.

beats.caption: The IDS correlates the chain and unlocks the intrusion flag
beats.say: Now we ask the intrusion detection system what it saw. Four alerts, all from our attack machine, spanning recon and impact. The IDS correlates them into a single intrusion, and unlocks the flag.

beats.head: Correlation over count
beats.body:
• The value is not one alert, but the story: same source, recon then impact.
  • Correlation cuts through alert fatigue — it says this is a real intrusion.
  • It also gives responders the full timeline to scope and contain.
beats.say: The value here is not one alert, but the story the alerts tell together: the same source doing reconnaissance and then impact. Correlation cuts through alert fatigue and tells the defender that this is a real intrusion, not noise. It also hands the responder the full timeline they need to scope and contain the attack.

beats.caption: Submit the flag in the CybICS dashboard - on the attack machine
beats.say: We finish on the dashboard, opening the intrusion detection challenge and submitting the flag the IDS unlocked when it caught the chain.

beats.head: What we learned
beats.body:
• Intrusions are chains; detection is strongest when it correlates them.
  • Tie alerts to a source and a timeline, not just a count.
  • Correlation is what turns a stream of alerts into an actionable incident.
beats.say: To recap: intrusions are chains of activity, and detection is strongest when it correlates them rather than counting alerts in isolation. Tie the alerts to a source and a timeline, and you turn a stream of noise into a single actionable incident.

beats.say: Flag captured. Next we put on the forensic analyst's hat and read the full alert buffer to reconstruct the attack.
